findings.description: AC-004 states every valid rule set round-trips and AC-005 promises export then replace-import reproduces the rules, but the import cap is 1,000,000 bytes while AC-002 allows 1000 rules of up to 100 + 500 characters. A valid set of long non-ASCII rules (for example 1000 Cyrillic replacements of 500 characters, about 1.0-1.2 MB) exports a file that import refuses. No corruption results (import is atomic), but the guarantee is not universal.
findings.suggestion: Qualify AC-005: 'for an exported file within the import limit', or state that export refuses or warns when the file would exceed the import cap; keep the SC-002 1000-rule fixture under the cap.

citations.excerpt: Export then replace-import of the same file reproduces the same rules and order.

findings.description: The current wording of AC-006 and the Edge Cases limits the CJK exemption to base characters 'only'; a ZWNJ/ZWJ is not a base character, so the literal reading is that it blocks on a CJK side. The implementation on the branch ignores ZWNJ/ZWJ on a CJK side (comment in matcher.rs states so). Spec and code must agree; see the ambiguity ac-006:cjk-side-join-control.
findings.suggestion: Decide in Clarify. Recommended: a ZWNJ/ZWJ adjacent to the match blocks on a CJK side like a combining mark (false negative only, consistent with the deferred UAX #29 rule); add before/after fixtures.

citations.excerpt: the CJK exemption ignores neighbouring base characters only
the CJK side exemption applies to base characters only. A combining mark immediately next to the matched text still blocks the match, even on a CJK side.

findings.description: AC-007 says that without AI post-processing the inserted text includes the replacements, but the same criterion orders filler removal and normalization after replacement and protects replaced spans only from approximate correction. A replacement containing a filler word or a repeated word can be altered before insertion, so the inserted-text clause is not an exact oracle.
findings.suggestion: State that the guarantee is exact for the matcher output and the text handed to approximate correction; later filler removal and normalization apply to replacement text as to any text.

citations.excerpt: before the existing approximate custom-word correction, filler removal, normalization and AI post-processing
without AI post-processing, the inserted text includes them too
